description: 88 M03B-REWRITE VALUE 'Z' (app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL:108) reaches 2000-XREFFILE-PROC as a declared-but-dead operation, performs no I/O whatsoever, and reports the stale FILE STATUS the preceding end-of-file READ left in this file's own status area. Four calls in one session: OPEN INPUT, a READ that succeeds, a READ that hits end of file, then 'Z'. THE ARM. EVALUATE LK-M03B-DD (:118) tests its arms in source order - 'TRNXFILE' (:119), 'XREFFILE' (:121), 'CUSTFILE' (:123), 'ACCTFILE' (:125) - and :122 performs 2000-XREFFILE-PROC THRU 2999-EXIT. Reaching the second arm is evidence that 'TRNXFILE' was tested and rejected and that control did not fall into WHEN OTHER (:127-128), whose GO TO 9999-GOBACK jumps past every nnn900-EXIT and would therefore leave LK-M03B-RC stale rather than set - the outcome case19 pins. Arm order is behaviour, not presentation (gate G30, rule R7). CALL 1 - THE OPEN. IF M03B-OPEN (:159) is true, so OPEN INPUT XREF-FILE (:160) runs and GO TO 2900-EXIT (:161) leaves the paragraph before any later guard is reached; 2900-EXIT (:175-176) MOVEs XREFFILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC and 2999-EXIT (:178-179) EXITs. A successful OPEN INPUT yields '00', and the record area is untouched by an OPEN, so it comes back as the 1000 spaces the caller supplied. CALL 2 - THE READ THAT SUCCEEDS. IF M03B-OPEN (:159) is now false and IF M03B-READ (:164) is true, so READ XREF-FILE INTO LK-M03B-FLDT (:165) runs, then END-READ (:166), GO TO 2900-EXIT (:167) and :176. The INTO phrase copies the whole 50-byte record into the 1000-byte area and leaves the remaining 950 bytes as the spaces the caller moved in, so the image is the record left-justified in the area rather than a 50-byte value. FILE STATUS '00'. CALL 3 - THE READ THAT HITS END OF FILE. Exactly one row is seeded, so the second sequential READ finds nothing, sets XREFFILE-STATUS to '10' and leaves the record area untouched. That the area is returned UNCHANGED rather than blanked is an assertion with content here and not a tautology over 1000 spaces, because this call deliberately arrives with the previous record still in it: CBSTM03A issues MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC before effectively every call but issues MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT only at some sites (app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:350, :376, :400, :745, :834) and not at others (:857-860). A translation that cleared the receiver on a failed read would still show '10' here, and only the record area would give it away. For this DD the '10' is not an error at all - 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT (:345-361) EVALUATEs WS-M03B-RC with a '00' arm, a '10' arm that MOVEs 'Y' TO END-OF-FILE (:357-358) and only then WHEN OTHER, so '10' is how the caller's browse terminates normally. That is the opposite of the ACCTFILE EVALUATE at :392-414, which has neither a '10' nor a '23' arm and sends any non-'00' status straight to DISPLAY 'ERROR READING ACCTFILE' (:407) and PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM. CALL 4 - THE DEAD OPERATION, WHICH IS WHAT THIS CASE EXISTS FOR. 88 M03B-REWRITE VALUE 'Z' is declared at :108 and is SET nowhere in app/cbl - neither CBSTM03A nor any other program ever requests it - all four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT (:31-53), and no paragraph in CBSTM03B contains a REWRITE statement or a WRITE statement at all: the only textual occurrences of either word in the program are the two 88-level declarations at :107 and :108. The operation is therefore dead code, and practice B5 requires that it stay dead rather than be quietly given the behaviour its name suggests. Gate G48 nonetheless requires every one of the six declared operation codes to be exercised, and this is the suite's only 'Z' call, so the code is covered as the no-op it is. A 'Z' request matches IF M03B-OPEN (:159) no, IF M03B-READ (:164) no, IF M03B-CLOSE (:170) no, and falls through to 2900-EXIT (:175) having performed no I/O; :176 then MOVEs whatever XREFFILE-STATUS already holds, which is still the '10' the end-of-file READ wrote there. Reporting '10' rather than '00' is precisely what distinguishes a genuine no-op from a call that quietly succeeded, and it is only assertable because the caller reset LK-M03B-RC to '00' immediately beforehand - so the '10' in this image can have come from nowhere but the file's own status area. The record area likewise comes back exactly as call 3 left it, because a path that writes back nothing but the status cannot have assigned a record. THE PAIR OF DEAD CODES. case17 drives the other one, 'W' (:107), on ACCTFILE after a keyed read that missed, so it reports a stale '23'; this case drives 'Z' on XREFFILE after a browse that ran out, so it reports a stale '10'. Two dead operation codes, two different stale statuses, two different status areas - and in both cases the seeded dataset is pinned afterwards to prove that nothing reached it. The same three-call prefix followed by a LIVE operation is case08, whose CLOSE is implemented at :170-173; setting the two side by side is what shows that falling through the guard chain and being handled by it are different outcomes. NO KEY IS READ ON THIS DD. XREFFILE is ORGANIZATION INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY IS FD-XREF-CARD-NUM (:37-41), so 2000-XREFFILE-PROC guards only M03B-OPEN, M03B-READ and M03B-CLOSE and has no IF M03B-READ-K at all; the MOVE LK-M03B-KEY (1:LK-M03B-KEY-LN) statement that would read the key span exists only at :189 for CUSTFILE and :214 for ACCTFILE. LK-M03B-KEY therefore stays 25 spaces and LK-M03B-KEY-LN stays '000{' on all four rows, supplied by the caller and never inspected by the subroutine. THE ZONED KEY LENGTH. LK-M03B-KEY-LN is PIC S9(4) (:111), a signed zoned item whose sign is overpunched into the low-order byte, so the length 0 that a non-keyed call carries renders as the image '000{' - a brace, being a positive digit zero - and never as '0000' and never as a JSON number. THE STATUS AREA (gate G47). XREFFILE-STATUS (:87-89) is the second of four independent two-byte areas (:83-97), none of which carries a VALUE clause, so every status pinned here belongs to that area alone and says nothing about TRNXFILE-STATUS, CUSTFILE-STATUS or ACCTFILE-STATUS. That independence is exactly what makes the stale '10' of call 4 meaningful: it is the same storage the READ of call 3 wrote, not a shared or re-initialised one. THE WIDTHS, re-derivable by hand (practice B11). LK-M03B-AREA is 1040 = 8 + 1 + 2 + 25 + 4 + 1000 (:100-112), and each of the four images below is pinned at that width both field by field and as a whole. The XREFFILE record is 50 = 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 from app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy, and the FD split at :65-68 confirms it independently as 16 + 34. THE FIXTURE PAD (gate G16, risk R-F). app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt carries 36 bytes per row where CVACT03Y declares 50, because the fixture omits the trailing FILLER X(14) - it is the one fixture of the nine whose width does not match its copybook. The row is right-padded to 50 before comparison, declared here as the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation so the pad has a single owner on the seeding side; that pad and USRSEC 57 to 80 are the suite's only two. THE RECORD DECODE. The seeded row is pinned across all four CVACT03Y spans in declaration order rather than only as a byte image, because FieldDiffer compares field by field (gate G17) and a whole-string compare would hide a misplaced boundary inside a span - two adjacent numeric spans, XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) and XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11), are exactly where such a boundary would hide. Both are pinned as characters with their leading zeros intact, '000000050' and '00000000050', and never as JSON numbers, because a value must not be re-scaled or reparsed merely by being loaded; both spans are unsigned, so neither carries an overpunch. The trailing FILLER X(14) is pinned as 14 spaces because omitting it would leave the record 36 bytes long instead of 50 (gates G19 and G21). READ-ONLY PROOF. All four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT and no paragraph writes, so the seeded dataset is read back after the run and pinned row for row, unchanged, and its FINAL_STATE row count and 50-byte record length are pinned too. That assertion matters more on this case than on any other in the folder: a translation that let the dead 'Z' fall into a real REWRITE would leave the file altered while every LK-M03B-RC still looked exactly right, and no area image could reveal it. WHAT IS NOT HERE. expectedReturnCode is 0 because CBSTM03B contains no RETURN-CODE reference and no CALL statement - it GOBACKs (:130-131) without ever touching one - and because LK-M03B-RC is a two-byte FILE STATUS, not a return code: the '10' above must not be read as one. expectedMessages is empty because the program contains no DISPLAY statement at all; 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' belongs to its caller (app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:359), as do 'ERROR OPENING XREFFILE' (:774) and 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE' (:882). jobParameters is empty because CBSTM03B is a @Component and not a Spring Batch Job despite the ...Job name the plan assigns it (gate G12, requirement I3), because it is never reached through a JobLauncher or over HTTP (gate G51), and because job parameters belong to a BATCH_JOB alone - the four-call script this case describes therefore lives beside the other nineteen in CBSTM03BParityTest, since ParityCase carries inputs and expectations but no script. Every byte is US-ASCII, the code page of the authoritative app/data/ASCII fixtures, and never a platform default (practice B8). PROVENANCE (practice B12). Every expected value above was derived statically - by structured reading of the line numbers cited, the CVACT03Y byte offsets and the real bytes of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt - and was never captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the COBOL. That execution is empirically impossible here: cobc refuses CBSTM03B at :114 because PROCEDURE DIVISION USING is a subprogram entry rather than an executable main, its indexed file handler is reported disabled, which excludes all four of these ORGANIZATION INDEXED files, and no Language Environment CEE service exists. AAP section 0.7.6 records the eight verified blockers and section 0.9.11 escalates the deviation as risk R-A: only the provenance of these values changes - the 20 cases per program this file is one of (gate G15), field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate per module (gate G18) all stand.
